1. In the Bharatiya ethos, the Vedic, Jainas, and Buddhist Darsanas described geometrical models of the universe and the terrestrial earth. It is remarkable to mention here that the Siddhanta texts give theories of established principles in the
field of astronomy and cosmology. The Bhugolädhyaya of Sürya Siddhanta discusses the creation of the universe and earth, and the evolution of pañcamahabhutas. The Brhat Samhita of Varahamihira describes cosmic evolution. These texts also deal with directions in space, parts of time; i.e. past, present, and future. The concepts of genesis of universe given in the astronomical texts are the similar as those given in most of the Bhãratiya philosophical schools.
In the ancient Bhäratiya thought, the genesis of the universe is termed as Vedic cosmology"'. According to this concept, the creation is only a manifestation of the
Supreme Being (Brahman). Befor creation, the Brahman existed in an un-manifested form. The state being before creation is described in detail in the
Mendel's studies mainly described those traits that have distinct alternate forms such as flower colour which are either purple or white. But if you look around you will find that there are many traits which are not so distinct in their occurrence and are spread across a gradient. For example, in humans we don't just have tall or short people as two distinct alternatives but a whole range of possible heights. Such traits are generally controlled by three or more genes and are thus called as polygenic traits. Besides the involvement of multiple genes polygenic inheritance also takes into account the influence of environment. Human skin colour is another classic example for this. In a polygenic trait the phenotype reflects the contribution of each allele, i.e., the effect of each allele is additive. To understand this better let us assume that three genes A, B, C control skin colour in human with the dominant forms A, B and C responsible for dark skin colour and the recessive forms a, b and c for light skin colour. The genotype with all the dominant alleles (AABBCC) will have the darkest skin colour and that with all the recessive alleles (aabbcc) will have the lightest skin colour. As expected the genotype with three dominant alleles and three recessive alleles will have an intermediate skin colour. In this manner the number of each type of alleles in the genotype would determine the darkness or lightness of the skin in an individual.

The pursuit of science is a combination of great elation and great despair. I went over many such episodes in my mind. Johannes Kepler, whose three orbital laws form the basis of space research, took nearly 17 years after formulating the two laws about planetary motion around the sun, to enunciate his third law which gives the relation between the size of the elliptical orbit and the length of time it takes for the planet to go around the sun. How many failures and frustrations must he have gone through? The idea that man could land on the moon, developed by the Russian mathematician Konstantin
Tsiolkovsky, was realised after nearly four decades- and by the United States, at that.
Prof. Chandrasekhar had to wait nearly 50 years before receiving the Nobel Prize for his discovery of the 'Chandrasekhar Limit', a discovery made while he was a graduate student at Cambridge in the 1930s. If his work had been recognized then, it could have led to the discovery of the Black Hole decades earlier. How many failures must Von
Braun have gone through before his Saturn launch vehicle put man on the moon? These thoughts helped to give me the ability to withstand apparently irreversible setbacks.

(a) Time is the most precious resource available to mankind. Unlike money or material possessions, time once lost can never be recovered. Every second that passes is gone forever. Successful people in the world are those who understand the value of every
moment and use it wisely. Time management is not just about doing more work, but about doing the right work at the right time.
Procrastination, which means delaying tasks for tomorrow, is the greatest enemy of success. Many students and professionals fail to achieve their goals because they do not respect time. Life is short, and we have many responsibilities to fulfil. If we waste time in idle gossip or unproductive activities, we miss the opportunities that life offers us. A punctual person is always respected in society.
Nature also teaches us the importance of time. The sun rises and sets on time, and the seasons change according to their schedule. We must learn to discipline ourselves and create a balance between work and rest. Remember, time waits for no one. Those who master time master their lives. Therefore, start valuing your time today to build a better and brighter future.

(15) Fresh snowfall in many areas of the higher reaches of Kashmir has led to the closure of two national highways, while rains lashed the valley's plains. Bandipora district in Jammu and
Kashmir received fresh snowfall, prompting authorities to close the Bandipora-Gurez road as a precaution. The plains of the valley, including Srinagar city, were lashed by moderate, widespread rains, with intermittent rainfall at several places. The night temperature was three to five degrees above normal across the valley. There is a possibility of moderate snow over a few higher reaches of north and central Kashmir.
A massive rush of tourists was witnessed on Sunday at the Gulmarg Gondola, with long queues reported at ticket counters and boarding points as visitors thronged the popular destination following fresh snowfall. Hundreds of tourists were seen standing in long lines for hours to access the cable car service, one of the highest in the world, which operates in two phases, connecting Gulmarg to Kongdoori and then to Apharwat.
